_README:
The single source of the book's structure; the build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. Authored from book.draft.json (scripts/ingest_epub.py). The source EPUB split its one text file mechanically into part0000_split_NNN.html chunks that DO line up one-to-one with the logical chapters (each chunk opens with a

heading). ch01 is the prologue (楔子), ch02..ch13 are the twelve numbered chapters. Chapter ids start with 'ch'. A chapter is treated as translated once out/_reading.md exists.

description: The first volume of Gu Long's Lu Xiaofeng saga. Lu Xiaofeng -- the idle, quick-witted swordsman famed for the two extra 'eyebrows' of his moustache and for the Spirit-Skewering Finger that can catch a blade between two fingertips -- is drawn into the intrigue of a fallen kingdom, a vanished dynasty of the Golden Roc, a princess seeking vengeance, and a killer hidden among friends. A locked-room mystery told at a swordsman's pace, with the swordsmen Ximen Chuixue and the blind, gentle Hua Manlou at his side.
_source_note: Source: a 2013 Henan Literature and Art Publishing House digital EPUB of 陆小凤传奇·1·金鹏王朝 (from the 古龙文集 collected-works line; the source's own calibre title-sort is 古龙文集·陆小凤传奇１：金鹏王朝). Simplified characters throughout. The novel itself was first serialised 1976-77; the translator's note states the composition date so the 2013 metadata is not read as the work's date. The spine has 18 documents; only 13 carry the book (ch01-ch13 below). Excluded, and what became of each: titlepage.xhtml (cover image, reused byte-identical as the EPUB cover); part0000_split_000.html and _001.html (9-char half-title stubs, each nothing but the running title 陆小凤：金鹏王朝 13-03-07 副本 plus a decorative endpaper image, dropped); part0000_split_002.html (the CIP / copyright colophon -- data captured in source_ref and rights, page dropped); part0000_split_003.html (the source table of contents 目录, regenerated natively by the builder). Images: cover.jpeg is the cover; 00001.jpeg and 00002.jpeg are decorative publisher endpapers (alt text 知识小说环衬) with no story content -- NOT carried into figures.json. The book has NO images of its own and NO source-edition footnotes (grep for [\d+] over every unit returns none; recorded in PROGRESS.md). In the final chapter (ch13, the Coda) the source text carries two trailing publisher lines that are NOT story text and are EXCLUDED from the translated chapter body (as the half-title stubs were): the volume-end marker 《陆小凤传奇：金鹏王朝》完 ('The Legend of Lu Xiaofeng: The Golden Roc Dynasty ends') and a next-volume pointer 相关情节请看《陆小凤传奇2：绣花大盗》 ('for the related tale, see The Legend of Lu Xiaofeng 2: The Embroidery Bandit'). Both are surfaced, not dropped: they are recorded here and rendered to the reader in the closing translator's footnote on the Coda's last paragraph.
_translator_note: Rendered verbatim as the Translator's Note back-matter page.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 金鹏王朝 (The Golden Roc Dynasty), the first volume of Gu Long's Legend of Lu Xiaofeng (陆小凤传奇). Gu Long (古龙, 1938-1985) first serialised it in 1976-77; this translation was made from a 2013 Henan Literature and Art Publishing House digital edition of the collected-works text.

The aim is a translation that reads as the wuxia entertainment it is -- fast, spare, and wry, built from Gu Long's characteristic short paragraphs and abrupt line breaks -- while a Western reader with no background in Chinese martial-arts fiction still catches what the original assumes: the conventions of the jianghu, the martial sects and their rivalries, the weights and money, the courtesies and their violations. Footnotes supply that context; a glossary collects recurring names and terms; and where the source is ambiguous or its digitisation is corrupt, the note says so rather than smoothing it over.
Names are given in Hanyu Pinyin without tone marks (Lu Xiaofeng, Ximen Chuixue, Hua Manlou). Where a name carries meaning the plot turns on, the meaning is glossed at first appearance.
_structure_note:
One entry per logical unit, in reading order. ch01 = the prologue; ch02..ch13 = numbered chapters 1..12 (the source labels its closing chapter 第十二竡 尾声, a coda, and its opening piece 楞子, a prologue). Only the prologue carries named internal sections (four vignettes, each a

title line); chapters 1-12 divide themselves with bare numeric markers (01, 02, ...) that are scene breaks, not titled sections -- they render as '***' via apply_format_markers.py, not as TOC entries. 'chars' is the source character count from ingest (chapter 11, 第六根足趾, is the long climax at ~31k). 'src' is the spine href; 'text_file' the extracted source text.
